text: OrthogonalMatchingPursuit reproducibility with OpenBLAS and different number of cores We've been experiencing reproducibility issues with _OrthogonalMatchingPursuit_ in different computing environments. The output has been very stable for us when running on hosts with two cores, but we noticed we were getting different results on hosts with eight cores. The two result sets are stable, but different. Searching the project's issues it looks like there was some OMP reproducibility issues in the CI environment around 2014, which led to the OMP tests being disabled. Looking at the code, there isn't a lot of potential culprits explaining such a behavior. [Parallel/delayed](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/master/sklearn/linear_model/_omp.py#L901) is used in _OrthogonalMatchingPursuitCV_, but can be controlled with n_jobs and this doesn't change the outcome. Diving deeper brings us to scipy's use of OpenBLAS. We noticed the sklearn test suite is running with `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2` [in CI](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/master/.travis.yml#L17). Setting this environment variable in the 8 cores environment solved our reproducibility issue. So now to the questions: - is this a known OpenBLAS issue? - are the results with `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2` more correct than without with more than two cores or are the results different but equally valid? - what are the performance implications of running sklearn with `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2`?
label: bug

text: `CalibratedClassifierCV(method="sigmoid")` should always take the raw logits as inputs instead of the predicted probabilities This is a defect [I first observed while reviewing the temperature scaling PR](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/31068#discussion_r2012459507): if the uncalibrated classifier only exposes a `decision_function` and no `predict_proba` (which is the case for SVMs for instance) our implementation of sigmoid calibration (aka Platt-scaling) is fine because the output values of `decision_function` are morally logits between -inf and +inf with 0 as the default decision threshold. But if the uncalibrated classifier already exposes a `predict_proba` method (e.g. `GaussianNB`), our current implementation takes the predicted probabilities as input of the parametrized sigmoid function. text: r2_score metric incorrect? Hello, The r2_score metric is something that many functions in sklearn use but right now I think it generally is set as 1 - RSS/SYY, which would the right formula to use if you run a regression with an intercept. If you did not use this, however, and ran a regression with no intercept then the r2_score should be equal to (y_pred^2).sum()/(y_true^2).sum() and notice that we do not demean. Moreover, for other models, 1 - RSS/SYY might be negative or not between 1 and 0, which again is bad. For a standard regression with an intercept term, 1 - RSS/SYY = corr(y_pred,y_true)^2 and this number, no matter what the model is, is between 0 and 1 with 1 as the goal. I think the definition should then be changed on a per model basis or it should be changed to corr(y_pred,y_true)**2. The book "Applied Linear Regression" by S Weisberg mentions the issue I address above on page 84 of the third edition. It suggest to use corr(y_pred,y_true)^2 for nonlinear models and to alternate the definition as above for regression through the origin. Finally, with regards to regression, statsmodels does use a different formula for the r2_score depending on if you use or do not use the intercept in a regression. Maybe this is known already, but the codebase does not seem to differentiate at all so that's why I am putting the issue here. Thanks!
label: bug

The docstring in `sklearn/metrics/pairwise.py` says it calculates distances up to: `"(X[0], Y[0]), (X[1], Y[1]), ..., (X[n_samples], Y[n_samples])."` Because Python starts counting at 0, the last item in an array of size `n_samples` is actually at `n_samples - 1`. If we try to use `X[n_samples]` in real code, Python throws an `IndexError`. ### Steps/Code to Reproduce Here is a quick code example using the docstring's own matrix shape to show the error: ```python import sklearn import numpy as np print(f"Scikit-Learn Version: {sklearn.__version__}") n_samples = 3 X = np.array([[1, 1, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]]) try: X[n_samples] except IndexError as e: print(f"Error: {e}") # Output: Error: index 3 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 3 ``` `Scikit-Learn Version: 1.8.0` ### Suggest a potential alternative/fix To fix this, we just need to update the docstring in `sklearn/metrics/pairwise.py` to end with `(X[n_samples - 1], Y[n_samples - 1])`. Let me know if I should open a quick PR to patch this!

As a result, the model reports its lowest uncertainty at the coordinate origin rather than at the center of the training data.
